Several hours for the missions and the Magma Bubble (includes a trip to Marapur); climbing the Hazard System takes several days, because the Primal Menace can only be killed once every 20 h

The gnomes have discovered {wiki:Gnomprona|Gnomprona}, an underground island next to a volcano beneath Marapur, and the volcano's seismic activity is worrying them. Enlist with the {npc:Gnomcruiter} in Edron and help {npc:Gnominer} with six tasks (scout fairies, flame charges, fire fields, magma crystals, the nagas' artefact and resonance crystals) until you face the {creature:Magma Bubble} with up to 5 players. You earn the base {wiki:Fire-Fighter Outfits|Fire-Fighter} outfit and access to the **Hazard System**, where {creature:The Primal Menace} can give you the {wiki:Ripptor|Ripptor} mount and a piece of the {wiki:Primal Set|Primal Set}.
The gnomes have discovered a wonderful place in the depths of the world and need help exploring it.

{wiki:Within the Tides Quest|Within the Tides Quest} completed (missions *Coastal Concerns*, *Mountainous Matters*, *Of Feathers and Flowers* and *Star-Crossed Lovers*): it gives you access to Marapur and the nagas' trust, without which you cannot do the *Snakes on a Plain!* mission.

For {creature:Magma Bubble}: a team of **up to 5 players** (blocker, shooters and mages). You can do the other missions alone (in *Raiders of the Lost Flame!* up to 5 can enter, but progress is individual).
Optional part (Hazard System): having defeated Magma Bubble and a strong team for {creature:The Primal Menace}.
50 gp from Gnomfurry; melts after 2 hours (Fairy Trails! mission)

Magma Bubble: **fire** and **physical** protection; **ice** and **death** damage (and **earth** only for the End of Days phase)
the best area rune against the Primal Menace
for the shooters to hit the Primal Menace

recommended for shooters at the Primal Menace

On the higher hazards: {wiki:Tibiadrome|Tibiadrome} potions (Amplification and Resilience) and {wiki:Strike Enhancement}
160 oz of free capacity to receive the {item:Primal Bag} (hazard 12 reward)

Access to Gnomprona's **Hazard System** and to the boss {creature:The Primal Menace}

when you reach hazard 12; it turns into a random Primal Set piece
Steamship trip from Cormaya to Gnomprona
Mission *The Island that time forgot!*: after you say {key:join} to the {npc:Gnomcruiter}, {npc:Gurbasch} takes you to Gnomprona ({key:gnomprona}).
Gnomprona and the Monster Graveyard, Crystal Enigma and Sparkling Pools hunting places
Mission *The Island that time forgot!*: when you reach the Gnomprona hub by Steamship; the hunting places are around the hub (ore wagons).
Mission *Magmageddon!*: after defeating the {creature:Magma Bubble}, talk to {npc:Gnominer}.
The addons are earned by using the {item:Firefighting Axe} and the {item:Portable Flame}, loot from the Magma Bubble.
After defeating the Magma Bubble, talk to {npc:Gnomadness}.
You choose the hazard level with Gnomadness; more loot and experience (+4% per level) in the Gnomprona hunting places.
After the Magma Bubble, through {npc:Gnomadness}; teleport at the far north end of the Monster Graveyard.
When you reach hazard 6 (beat the Primal Menace on hazard 5): say {key:mount} to {npc:Gnomadness}.
To receive **and** hand in each mission, always say {key:hi} and {key:challenger} to {npc:Gnominer}.

The Gnomprona hub is a **safe zone**. The three hunting areas ({wiki:Monster Graveyard}, {wiki:Crystal Enigma} and {wiki:Sparkling Pools}) have extremely strong creatures (the wiki recommends level 600 to hunt there) and can leave you rooted or feared.

The **ore wagons** south of Gnomfurry lead to the three areas: **left** = Monster Graveyard, **middle** = Crystal Enigma, **right** = Sparkling Pools. The Gnomprona map (section 1) shows the hunting areas floor (the three areas, Magma Bubble's volcano, the Primal Menace and the fairies on that floor); the task rooms are on the floor below, the wagons floor: go by the coordinates in each step.
The {item:Candy Lure} melts 2 hours after you buy it: only buy it when you are actually going to look for the fairies.
In the *Raiders of the Lost Flame!* mission you only have 10 minutes and, if you fail, you have to wait 20 hours to try again. Read the Blocking Stalagmite tip before you go in.
Magma Bubble and the Primal Menace have a **20-hour cooldown** each.
For the *Snakes on a Plain!* mission you go to Marapur through the portal at the top of the {wiki:Kha'zeel Mountains|Kha'zeel Mountains}: bring {spell:Levitate}.
1. The Island that time forgot! — enlist and reach Gnomprona
Gnomprona is an underground island beneath Marapur. You get there by {wiki:Steamship} from {wiki:Cormaya}, the island south of Edron, after enlisting with the gnome recruiter in Edron.

If you are not in **Edron**, take a boat: talk to the harbour captain in your city (for example {npc:Captain Bluebear} in Thais) and say {key:hi}, {key:edron}, {key:yes}. You arrive at the Edron harbour, next to {npc:Captain Seahorse}.

Go to the seven ivory towers of the {wiki:Noodles Academy of Modern Magic|Noodles Academy of Modern Magic}, in the **east** part of Edron. {npc:Gnomcruiter} is **1 floor above** ground level. Say {key:hi}, {key:talented}, {key:yes} and {key:join}: you are enlisted in the gnomes' expedition and he sends you to talk to {npc:Gnominer}, the head of operations in Gnomprona.
Go back to Edron harbour and talk to {npc:Captain Seahorse}: {key:hi}, {key:cormaya}, {key:yes} (20 gp). You land at the **north** harbour of {wiki:Cormaya}.
Go down to the Cormaya Steamship

The Cormaya {wiki:Steamship} is **8 floors below** the island. The stairs are beneath the **Cormaya Garden**, the garden **south** of the pier, behind and just **east** of the guildhall *Castle of the White Dragon*. Go all the way down: {npc:Gurbasch} is at the end of Cormaya Street, opposite the house *Cormaya 11*.
If you are in **Kazordoon**, you can also take {npc:Brodrosch}'s Steamship ({key:hi}, {key:cormaya}, {key:yes}; 160 gp): you arrive directly at Gurbasch's pier, without going through Edron.

Talk to {npc:Gurbasch}: {key:hi}, {key:gnomprona}, {key:yes}. The boat drops you at the pier of the Gnomprona hub, next to the captain, {npc:Urks The Mute}. The hub is a **safe zone**; {npc:Gnominer} is just **south** of the boat.
Map of Gnomprona (hunting areas floor): Monster Graveyard, Crystal Enigma, Sparkling Pools, Magma Bubble's volcano, the Primal Menace and the fairies on that floor

If you pay for Steamship trips with large coins (for example just one {item:Crystal Coin}), make sure you have room and capacity for the change: otherwise you still travel, but the change stays on the boat.
2. Fairy Trails! — the seven scout fairies
{npc:Gnominer} sent fairies to measure the seismic activity around the volcano, but seven have gone missing. You have to find them and "remind them of their duty" with sweets.
In the hub, just south of the boat, talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi} and {key:challenger}. **{key:challenger}** is the word you will use throughout the quest to receive and hand in missions.
Head **south** to {npc:Gnomfurry}, by the entrance to the wagons area. Say {key:hi} and {key:trade} and buy **one** {item:Candy Lure} (50 gp). The fairies only accept this sweet.
The sweet starts melting as soon as you buy it and lasts **2 hours**. If it melts, buy another one.

Enter the cave next to {npc:Gnomfurry} and head **south**. You will find **ore wagons** to three places: the **left** one leads to the {wiki:Monster Graveyard} area, the **middle** one to the {wiki:Crystal Enigma} area and the **right** one to the {wiki:Sparkling Pools} area. To return to the hub, do the route in reverse (wagon and Gnomfurry's cave).
The 3 fairies in the stone passages
Three {wiki:Lazyfairy|Lazyfairies} are in the **creature-free stone passages** where the wagons drop you. Go to each one and **use the {item:Candy Lure} on the fairy**.
The 4 fairies in the hunting areas
The other **four** fairies are on the **floor above**, inside the hunting areas, so you will have to deal with the creatures. Use the {item:Candy Lure} on each one.
Earth, death and fire protection; attack with ice
Earth and energy protection; attack with ice
Physical, energy and fire protection; attack with ice
Physical, energy and fire protection; attack with ice

The creatures in these areas are roughly as strong as those in the {wiki:Secret Library|Secret Library}, and the local special mechanics (Hazard System: criticals, {wiki:Primal Pod|Primal Pods} and {creature:Fungosaurus}) can be very dangerous. In the Monster Graveyard there is a creature that roots, in the Crystal Enigma one that causes fear (feared) and in the Sparkling Pools another one that roots.
The four fairies on the hunting areas floor are marked with yellow circles
With all seven fairies done, go back to the hub the same way (wagon and Gnomfurry's cave) and talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}. He gives you the next mission.
Gnominer sends you to collect flame charges at the **Moss** excavation site. Up to 5 players can enter, but progress is **individual**: each player has to do their own 3 charges.
Go to the Moss excavation site

Go down to the wagons through {npc:Gnomfurry}'s cave. The **Moss** excavation site is on the wagons floor, at the coordinate below; it is not documented which of the three wagons is closest, so go by the coordinate on the in-game map. Inside is {npc:Gnomish Operative (Moss)}.
You have **10 minutes** to complete the task. If you do not finish, you are kicked out of the room and can only try again after **20 hours**.
Clear a path to the flame

You have to reach the **other side of the room**. Kill the {creature:Blocking Stalagmite|Blocking Stalagmites} blocking your way and run from the {wiki:Raging Monster|Raging Monsters} and the {creature:Sulphur Menace|Sulphur Menaces}: their area attacks **push you back** and **use up the charges** you already have.
If you stand on the square where a Blocking Stalagmite spawns, it appears **south of you** and you can walk past it **diagonally** instead of killing it. That makes the task much faster.
Pick up and deliver the charges
On the other side, **step on the flame** to get a charge. Then go back to the **energy extractor**, at the start of the room, to deliver it. Repeat until you have delivered **3 charges**.
If an area attack hits you on the way back, you lose the charge you were carrying.
Leave the room, go back to the hub the same way and talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}.
Raiders of the Lost Flame! mission complete
Go to the Firefoot excavation site
Use the **right wagon** and go to the **Firefoot excavation site**. Inside is {npc:Gnomish Operative (Firefoot)}.

You have to reach the **structure at the far end** without stepping on **large fire fields**. The fields change gradually: first **ash**, then **small fire** and finally **large fire**. Only move onto fields that are not large fire yet and keep an eye on how they change.
If a large fire catches you, you are sent back to the entrance and can keep trying.
When you reach the end a **success message** appears on screen. Then **step on a large fire field** on purpose to go back to the entrance and leave through the **teleport**.
Go back to the hub by wagon and talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}.
Use the **right wagon** again and go to **site GT-M-01**. Inside is {npc:Gnomish Operative (GT-M-01)}.
Before moving on, use the **energy extractor** near the entrance. You get a **protective layer**, which shows as a number under your character's name.
Without protection, stepping on the fire fields takes **15% of your maximum health per second**.
Kill **3 {creature:Lesser Magma Crystal|Lesser Magma Crystals}**. While you walk through the fire, keep an eye on the protective layer number under your name.
Leave the room, go back to the hub by wagon and talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}. He tells you the gnomes' artefact is old and broken, but that the **nagas** have one.
In the Heat of the Fight mission complete
6. Snakes on a Plain! — the nagas' artefact (Marapur)

The gnomes cannot continue the experiment because their artefact is old and broken. Gnominer asks you to negotiate with the nagas of Marapur. This part requires the {wiki:Within the Tides Quest|Within the Tides Quest} completed.

Go back to the pier where you arrived and talk to {npc:Urks The Mute}, the captain of the Gnomprona boat. His dialogue and destinations are not documented: say {key:hi} and ask him where he can take you (the outbound boat came from **Cormaya**). If he drops you at the Cormaya Steamship, go up the Cormaya Garden stairs to the surface and go to the **north** harbour: {npc:Pemaret} takes you to Edron ({key:hi}, {key:edron}, {key:yes}; 20 gp).
Alternative: a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} takes you straight to your city's temple (it does not work in no-logout zones or with a logout block or protection zone block).

In Edron, talk to {npc:Captain Seahorse}: {key:hi}, {key:ankrahmun}, {key:yes} (160 gp). From **Ankrahmun**, leave the city to the **west** and climb on foot to the {wiki:Kha'zeel Mountains|Kha'zeel Mountains}, between Tiquanda and Ankrahmun, by the same route you took in the {wiki:Within the Tides Quest|Within the Tides Quest}.
Bring the {spell:Levitate} spell: in the Kha'zeel Mountains many paths to the upper floors can only be taken by levitating.
Climb to the top of the mountain (floor +5) and step into the **portal**: you are teleported to {wiki:Marapur|Marapur}. This is the access you gained in the Within the Tides Quest.

In Marapur, find the {npc:Nagging Naga} and ask about the {key:artifact}. Since you have already proven your loyalty to the nagas, they agree to send the artefact to the gnomes: answer {key:yes} to his question.
The nagas send the artefact to the gnomes

Go to the **Moonfall magic carpet** and talk to {npc:Ziyad}: say {key:hi} and ask about the destinations (magic carpets only serve Premium players). Choose **Edron**, if it is on the list, or a city with a boat to Edron.
Return to Gnomprona and hand in
Repeat the route from section 1: {npc:Captain Seahorse} ({key:cormaya}) → Cormaya Garden stairs → {npc:Gurbasch} ({key:gnomprona}). Talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}.
Snakes on a Plain! mission complete
The last test before the attack on the volcano. Here the charges are **shared**: what counts is the room's 10, no matter how many players are inside or who picks them up.
This time use the **left wagon** and enter the **teleport**.
{creature:Lava Puddle (Creature)|Lava Puddles} start appearing. Kill them: their remains are {item:Charged Flame|Charged Flames}. Pick them up.
Use each {item:Charged Flame} on one of the **green** **polarity reversed crystals**. A **crystal flame** lights up.

**Step on the crystal flame** to get a charge and then step on the **large crystal plate**, to the **south**, to deliver it. Repeat until the room has **10 charges**. When you are done a message appears in the centre of the room.
Leave the room, go back to the hub by wagon and talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}. With the artefact in place and all the tests done, the gnomes are ready to attack the volcano.

The final fight of the story. {creature:Magma Bubble} has **150,000** health, gives **80,000** experience, does not move, sees invisible creatures, is **immune to earth** and can only be killed **once every 20 hours** (Bosstiary: Archfoe). The fight uses the mechanics you practised in the tasks and has three phases.

Gather **up to 5 players** (a blocker/knight, shooters and mages). Equip **fire** and **physical** protection. Attack with **ice** and **death**; **earth** damage is only useful for the {creature:The End of Days|End of Days} phase, because Magma Bubble takes no earth damage.
Gain shield points and destroy the 3 Magma Crystals
Use the **right wagon**. The volcano entrance is in the {wiki:Sparkling Pools|Sparkling Pools} area, on the floor above (the same floor as the hub). Enter the volcano with your team.

The Sparkling Pools creatures ({creature:Emerald Tortoise}, {creature:Gore Horn}, {creature:Gorerilla}, {creature:Hulking Prehemoth}, {creature:Sabretooth (Creature)|Sabretooth}) use physical damage (also at range), energy and fire, and one of them roots. Go to the entrance together.
Inside the arena is the **Gnomish Crystallomancer**. Throughout the fight, **do not let the creatures attack him**.
If the gnome dies, the team **fails the fight**.

The 3 Magma Crystals are in an **overheated zone**. To be able to get in there you need shield points. Attack a {creature:The End of Days} until it is at **half health**: it fully heals itself and several {creature:Lava Creature|Lava Creatures} appear.
Unless the team can handle the damage from all the Lava Creatures, attack **one End of Days at a time** to control how many appear.

When the Lava Creatures die, they leave {item:Charged Flame|Charged Flames} on the ground. Pick them up **quickly** and use them on the crystals in the room that are **green** (they switch randomly between red and green, so run around the room looking for a green one before the flame disappears). Then **step on the purple flame** that appears: you get **5 shield points**, which appear below your character's name.

Gather several rounds of points: depending on the team's strength, at least **20 shield points across 4 players** (or more points on fewer players). Then enter the overheated zone and attack the {creature:Magma Crystal} until you destroy it. Repeat until all **three** are destroyed. You can also gather all the points you need at once and then go to the three overheated zones, one after the other.

Without a shield, the fire fields in the overheated zone take **60% of maximum health per second** as agony damage (it cannot be reduced): it is almost certain death. Keep **at least 5 points** so you can get out. Any crystals left alive slowly heal while the team gathers more points.
Phase 2 — the six End of Days

**Six** {creature:The End of Days} appear, but this time they no longer heal or spawn Lava Creatures. The blocker should take them to a spot where he can hold them all **facing the wall**, or block them **south of the crystal in the middle of the room**, so that none of them faces the shooters and the mages can use waves safely. Earth damage is useful here.

When the six die, the {creature:Magma Bubble} appears. It always summons **four {creature:Unchained Fire|Unchained Fires}**, so use **single-target** attacks on the boss. This phase is usually faster and simpler than the previous one. The knight must stop the Unchained Fires from **facing the boss**: their fire waves **greatly heal** the Magma Bubble.

The Unchained Fires deal a lot of area fire damage. The shooters should bring plenty of fire protection and stand **diagonally** to get hit less. The Magma Bubble also throws fireballs dealing around 407–556 damage.
80,000 experience and the Magma Bubble's loot
The boss can drop, among other things, the two items for the {wiki:Fire-Fighter Outfits|Fire-Fighter} addons and pieces of the primal sets. Values from the wiki's loot statistics (77 kills):

Primal Set pieces: {item:Alicorn Headguard}, {item:Alicorn Quiver}, {item:Charged Alicorn Ring}, {item:Arboreal Crown}, {item:Charged Arboreal Ring}, {item:Arboreal Tome}, {item:Arcanomancer Folio}, {item:Arcanomancer Regalia}, {item:Charged Arcanomancer Sigil}, {item:Spiritthorn Armor}, {item:Spiritthorn Helmet}, {item:Charged Spiritthorn Ring}, {item:Charged Ethereal Ring}

The exit from the boss arena is not documented. After the fight, leave the volcano the same way you came in and go back through the Sparkling Pools area and the **right-hand minecart** to the Gnomprona hub (safe zone).

Talk to {npc:Gnominer}: {key:hi}, {key:challenger}. You receive the base {wiki:Fire-Fighter Outfits|Fire-Fighter} outfit. The two addons are earned by using the {item:Firefighting Axe} and the {item:Portable Flame} that the Magma Bubble can drop (see the {wiki:Fire-Fighter Outfits Quest|Fire-Fighter Outfits Quest} guide).

Talk to {npc:Gnomadness}, the gnomes' chief scientist, in the hub. He gives you access to the **Hazard System** and to the boss {creature:The Primal Menace}. From here on everything is **optional**: the quest's story is over.
Access to the Hazard System and the Primal Menace

The Hazard System makes hunting in Gnomprona harder and more profitable. To be able to choose a higher hazard you must earn the corresponding **qualification** (your maximum hazard) by killing {creature:The Primal Menace}.

Each victory over the Primal Menace raises your qualification by **+1**, but **only if you kill it on the highest hazard you have already unlocked**. The Primal Menace has a **20-hour cooldown**, so levelling up takes several days.
In a party, the **lowest** hazard of all members counts. Anyone with a higher qualification than the rest of the team does not go up in that fight: try to all stay at the same level.

The hazard is **not applied automatically**. Talk to {npc:Gnomadness} and say the **number** of the hazard you want ({key:1}, {key:2}, etc.). You can choose a level below your maximum and change it whenever you like, **with no cooldown**. In Gnomprona, the effective hazard is shown in a counter below your character's name.
The higher the hazard, the more you gain and the more you risk:

Higher chance of appearing when you kill a creature. Always drops at least one item from the {wiki:Arboreal Set|Arboreal}, {wiki:Arcanomancer Set|Arcanomancer}, {wiki:Spiritthorn Set|Spiritthorn}, {wiki:Alicorn Set|Alicorn} or {wiki:Ethereal Set|Ethereal} sets
7.5% chance at every level; at hazard 1 the critical deals **+50%** damage and the extra increases with the level. You never take more than 1 critical from these creatures every 2 seconds
0.85% of attacks at hazard 1; from hazard 5 onwards it rises faster

Higher chance of them appearing when you kill creatures (at hazard 1: 0.875%) and more damage when you step on them in the 2nd phase (at hazard 1: 5% of current health + 500 ice damage). The number of pods also increases with the size of the group

{wiki:Primal Pod|Primal Pods} have three phases. In the **1st** (2 seconds) you can step on them and destroy them without taking damage. In the **2nd** (about 2 seconds) you still destroy them by stepping on them, but you take damage. In the **last** they turn into a {creature:Fungosaurus}. Always step on them as soon as they appear; when they are about to run out they start flashing yellow.
The Fungosaurus roots (rooted) and frightens (feared). It disappears if it is not killed within 5 minutes.

The boss that raises your hazard. The fight has two stages: with and without {wiki:Primal Pack Beast|Primal Pack Beasts}. The higher the hazard, the harder it gets: you take more damage, more pods appear and the boss dodges more often. It is a team fight (knight blocking, shooters and mages).
Take the **left-hand minecart** to the {wiki:Monster Graveyard} area, **go up the ramp** and keep heading **north** until you find the teleport.
Primal Menace teleport (north of the Monster Graveyard)

On the way you cross the Monster Graveyard ({creature:Sulphider}, {creature:Sulphur Spouter}, {creature:Nighthunter}, {creature:Stalking Stalk}, {creature:Undertaker}): earth, death and a lot of physical damage, plus a creature that roots.

Everyone: **earth** protection. The knight mainly against **death**; the shooters mainly against **energy**. The best area rune is the {item:Great Fireball Rune}. The shooters should wear a {item:Shockwave Amulet} (it protects against two of the three elements they take) and a {item:Might Ring} throughout the fight. Sorcerers and druids on permanent {spell:Magic Shield}.
Boss attacks: melee up to 763, Earth Wave 1518–2199, Fire Wave 968, Death Wave 258–276, Energy Strike 1213–1221 and Poison Missile 626–1811, as well as a chain attack and self-healing.
Without Pack Beasts: hit the boss

The knight keeps the boss **in the middle of the room**. The shooters spread out around it, watching where Primal Pods and Pack Beasts spawn, and hit the boss with {item:Sudden Death Rune|Sudden Death Runes}. Paladins: use a bow with {item:Diamond Arrow|Diamond Arrows} so you don't lose turns switching weapons. The mages save {spell:Hell's Core} and {spell:Eternal Winter} for the summons.
Whenever a {wiki:Primal Pod|Primal Pod} appears, whoever is closest (including the knight) runs to step on it straight away. One Fungosaurus too many greatly reduces your chances of winning.
With Pack Beasts: kill within 20 seconds

At a certain point the boss starts summoning {wiki:Primal Pack Beast|Primal Pack Beasts}. Each one must die within **20 seconds**, otherwise it turns into a {creature:Fungosaurus} with full health. **Always focus the Pack Beasts**: the Primal Menace dies little by little from the area damage and from the attacks made when there are no Pack Beasts alive.
The less health the boss has (or the higher the hazard), the more often Pack Beasts spawn and the more pods appear: the fight gets harder and harder.
Gathering the Pack Beasts on the knight

The knight approaches the Pack Beast that spawns and uses {spell:Challenge} as quickly as possible, then goes back to the middle. The shooters run to the side opposite the Pack Beast (so they don't pull its aggro) and help pull it towards the knight, so that everyone can hit it.
If the knight moves too much, some Pack Beasts switch targets; if he doesn't move at all, the shooters' lives get much harder. Find the balance.

The mages use waves **whenever they can**. Although the boss is immune to earth, the druids' {spell:Terra Wave} deals much more damage to the Pack Beasts than GFBs. The sorcerers' {spell:Great Fire Wave} and {spell:Energy Wave} deal a lot of damage to the Pack Beasts and to the boss. If a Pack Beast is about to turn into a Fungosaurus, use {spell:Hell's Core} and/or {spell:Eternal Winter} immediately.

Some teams bring two Sorcerers instead of two Druids, for more damage. This increases the risk for the knight and is usually only possible if the blocker and the remaining Druid are very strong (around level 1200+). Anyone who needs to recover mana can eat a {item:Blessed Steak}, {item:Blueberry Cupcake} or {item:Consecrated Beef} when their mana drops below ~10%.

The {creature:Fungosaurus} causes **fear (feared)**, so the knight loses mobility: he should use the {item:Fire Bomb Rune} so he doesn't run off at random. From then on it is up to the shooters to pull the Pack Beasts to the blocker.

Primal Pods that appear next to the knight wipe out the bomb fields: renew them. If there is **more than 1 Fungosaurus** in the fight, it is advisable to **leave the room**, or you risk the death of part or all of the team.

When the Primal Menace dies, the summons and the Fungosauruses disappear, but the **pods that already exist do not**: step on them or leave quickly. If all goes well, the fight lasts between 2 and 5 minutes. Your hazard qualification goes up by +1 (if you fought at your maximum level).

The exit from the boss room is not documented. After the fight, go back the same way you came in: cross the Monster Graveyard to the **south**, go down the ramp and take the **left-hand minecart** back to the hub.

For the last hazard levels it is worth everyone using {wiki:Tibiadrome|Tibiadrome} potions (**Amplification** and **Resilience**) and {wiki:Strike Enhancement}, to withstand the huge criticals and make up for the dodge of the Pack Beasts and the boss.
If you fail the fight after an investment like this, you lose everything you spent.

When you reach **hazard 6** (that is, after defeating the Primal Menace on **hazard 5**), talk to {npc:Gnomadness} and ask him for the mount: {key:hi}, {key:mount}. You receive the {wiki:Ripptor|Ripptor} (+10 speed) and the achievement **Ripp-Ripp Hooray!**.

When you reach **hazard 12** (after defeating the Primal Menace on **hazard 11**), talk to {npc:Gnomadness} and ask for the reward: {key:hi}, {key:reward}. You receive a {item:Primal Bag}, which a few seconds later turns into a random piece of the {wiki:Primal Set|Primal Set} (minimum level 400 to use).
The Primal Bag weighs **160 oz**: make sure you have free capacity before asking for it. The piece is random and may not be for your vocation.
A random piece of the Primal Set

Go back to the pier where you arrived and talk to {npc:Urks The Mute}, the captain of the Gnomprona boat. His conversation and destinations are not documented: say {key:hi} and ask him where he can take you (the outbound boat came from **Cormaya**). If he drops you at the Cormaya Steamship, you can continue with {npc:Gurbasch} to **Kazordoon** ({key:hi}, {key:kazordoon}, {key:yes}; 160 gp), or go up the stairs of the Cormaya Garden to the surface and head to the **north** harbour, where {npc:Pemaret} takes you to Edron ({key:hi}, {key:edron}, {key:yes}; 20 gp).
Alternative: a {item:Temple Teleport Scroll} takes you straight to your city's temple (it does not work in no-logout zones or with a logout block or protection zone block).

The quest and Gnomprona were added in version 12.90 (Summer Update 2022). In the story, this is where the gnomes discovered the **Exaltation Forge**: the gnome scientists got it working and the Adventurers' Guild took it to one of its bases.

Pieces of the {wiki:Primal Set|Primal Set} can also drop from the {creature:Magma Bubble} and the {creature:Plunder Patriarch} (which appears at random in Gnomprona's hunting areas, more often on high hazards, and always drops at least one piece).
The {wiki:Fire-Fighter Outfits Quest|Fire-Fighter Outfits Quest} guide explains how to get the two addons with the Magma Bubble's loot.
